quiz.title: T4.4: Performs Mathematical Operations and Date/Time Manipulation
quiz.description: Scenario-based questions on ObjectScript strict left-to-right evaluation (NO operator precedence), parentheses, modulo (#), integer division (\), weak typing, $HOROLOG, $ZDATE/$ZDATEH, $ZTIME, and date arithmetic.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the result of this expression:

"A" + "B"
questions.explanation: In ObjectScript, the + operator always performs numeric addition. Non-numeric strings like "A" and "B" are coerced to 0 (they have no leading numeric portion). So "A" + "B" = 0 + 0 = 0. String concatenation uses the _ operator: "A" _ "B" = "AB". No error is thrown because weak typing is a core feature of ObjectScript. (Reference: InterSystems Practice Q16; https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_numeric)

questions.question:
Which of the following expressions evaluates to 5?

Remember: ObjectScript evaluates strictly left-to-right with NO operator precedence.
questions.explanation:
Evaluating each left-to-right (parentheses evaluated first):
a) 2/2=1, +2=3, +4=7, /2=3.5
b) (2*3)=6, then 1+6=7, +1=8, /2=4
c) 2+4=6, *1=6, +1=7
d) (4*2)=8, (1+2)=3, then 3+4=7, +8=15, /3=5
Only option d equals 5. (Reference: InterSystems Practice Q17; https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_precedence)

questions.question:
A junior developer is surprised by this result. Consider:

write 2 + 3 * 4

What is the output?
questions.explanation: ObjectScript evaluates expressions strictly left-to-right with NO operator precedence. So: 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 * 4 = 20. In languages with standard math precedence, 3*4 would be evaluated first giving 14, but ObjectScript does not follow that convention. Use parentheses to control order: 2 + (3 * 4) = 14. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_precedence)

questions.question:
You are calculating a hash bucket for load balancing. Consider:

set bucket = 47 # 8
write bucket

What is the output?
questions.explanation: The # operator performs modulo (remainder) division. 47 # 8: 47 divided by 8 is 5 with remainder 7 (5 * 8 = 40, 47 - 40 = 7). So the result is 7. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_numeric)

questions.question:
You are calculating page numbers from a record offset. Consider:

set page = 47 \ 10
write page

What is the output?
questions.explanation: The \ operator performs integer division (truncates toward zero). 47 \ 10 = 4 (47 / 10 = 4.7, truncated to 4). This is useful for pagination and similar integer calculations. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_numeric)

questions.question:
You encounter the ObjectScript modulo operator with a negative number. Consider:

write -7 # 3

What is the output?
questions.explanation: In ObjectScript, the modulo operator (#) always returns a result with the same sign as the divisor (or zero). For -7 # 3: the result is 2 (because -7 = -3*3 + 2). This differs from languages like C where -7 % 3 = -1. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_numeric)

questions.question: What format does the $HOROLOG special variable use?
options: Two comma-separated integers: days since December 31, 1840 and seconds since midnight
questions.explanation: $HOROLOG contains the current local date and time as two comma-separated integers: the number of days since December 31, 1840, and the number of seconds since midnight. For example, "67891,45000" means day 67891 at 45000 seconds past midnight. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_vhorolog)

questions.question:
You are writing a time display utility. Consider:

set h = "67891,3661"
write $ZTIME($PIECE(h, ",", 2))

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $PIECE(h, ",", 2) extracts the seconds portion (3661). $ZTIME converts seconds since midnight to a time string. 3661 seconds = 1 hour + 1 minute + 1 second = "01:01:01" in the default 24-hour HH:MM:SS format. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fztime)

questions.question: You need to add 7 days to the current date and keep the result as a $HOROLOG day number. Which code does that?
questions.explanation: $HOROLOG is "days,seconds" (for example 67669,34384). Applying + to it makes ObjectScript read characters up to the first non-numeric one, so $HOROLOG + 7 yields the day count plus 7 -- the same value $PIECE($HOROLOG, ",", 1) + 7 computes explicitly, which is the clearer way to write it. $DATEADD is not an ObjectScript function. $SYSTEM.SQL.Functions.DATEADD does run and returns the right DATE, but as an ODBC timestamp string ('2026-09-24 00:00:00'), not the $HOROLOG day number the question asks for. $INCREMENT does not even compile against a special variable -- it raises <SYNTAX>, because it increments a stored node, not an expression.

questions.question:
You are converting an ODBC date string to $HOROLOG format. Consider:

set hDate = $ZDATEH("2026-03-05", 3)

What does hDate contain?
options: An integer representing days since December 31, 1840
questions.explanation: $ZDATEH is the inverse of $ZDATE - it converts a date string to a $HOROLOG date value. Format 3 = YYYY-MM-DD (ODBC/ISO). It returns an integer representing days since December 31, 1840, which can be used for date arithmetic. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fzdateh)

questions.question:
You are debugging a complex expression. Consider:

write 10 - 2 * 3 + 1

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Left-to-right evaluation: 10 - 2 = 8, then 8 * 3 = 24, then 24 + 1 = 25. Standard math precedence would give 10 - 6 + 1 = 5, but ObjectScript evaluates strictly left-to-right. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_precedence)

questions.question:
A report generator needs today's date in ISO format. Consider:

write $ZDATE($HOROLOG, 3)

What format does this produce?
questions.explanation: $ZDATE format 3 returns a date in YYYY-MM-DD format (ODBC/ISO 8601). Common formats: 1 = MM/DD/YYYY (US), 3 = YYYY-MM-DD (ISO), 4 = DD/MM/YYYY (European). Format 3 is the most common for database operations and international standards. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fzdate)

questions.question:
You are reviewing a billing calculation. Consider:

write 100 - 10 * 2 + 5 * 3

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Left-to-right: 100 - 10 = 90, * 2 = 180, + 5 = 185, * 3 = 555. This is a dangerous expression in ObjectScript because most developers expect standard precedence (100 - 20 + 15 = 95). Always use parentheses for clarity. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_precedence)

questions.question: Which of the following are special variables related to date and time in ObjectScript? (Select all that apply)
options: $HOROLOG - local date and time as days,seconds (integer precision)
$ZTIMESTAMP - UTC date and time with fractional seconds
$ZHOROLOG - local date and time with fractional seconds
questions.explanation: $HOROLOG contains local date,time as integer days and seconds. $ZTIMESTAMP contains UTC date,time with fractional seconds. $ZHOROLOG does NOT contain date/time — it contains the number of seconds elapsed since the most recent InterSystems IRIS startup. There are no $NOW or $DATE special variables in ObjectScript. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_vzhorolog)

questions.question:
A developer needs midnight represented as a time value. Consider:

write $ZTIME(0)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $ZTIME(0) converts 0 seconds since midnight to the default 24-hour time format: "00:00:00". The default format (tformat=1) is HH:MM:SS in 24-hour notation. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fztime)
